title: Plan, build a client-proof CMS, and launch properly

say: Plan the site, build a client-proof CMS, and launch it properly.
This is the video for module 2 of Webflow Development: Professional Build Workflow.

Rebuilding a section because the content did not fit costs far more than an hour of planning. First, the sitemap. A static page, like About, is designed once. A template page is designed once but shows any item from a Collection.

panel.heading: A build plan has three parts

cards.d: Which pages exist. Mark static pages and CMS template pages.
Which content repeats, and the fields each Collection needs.
A hidden page of headings, buttons and colours, stored as Variables.

say: Second, the content model. If the client says, we will add a new one every month, that content belongs in the CMS, with the right fields.

say: Third, a style guide page. Store colours and sizes as Variables, so when the brand colour changes, you change one variable and the whole site updates.

say: For example, Funmi runs an interior design studio in Abuja and adds about two projects a month. She needs 4 static pages.

panel.heading: Planning an interior design studio site
items: Static pages: Home, About, Services, Contact
Collections: Projects and Testimonials
Option field for project type; switch for Featured
4 static + 1 template = 5 designs to build

say: Projects repeat monthly, so they become a Collection. Testimonials too, linked to projects with a reference field. Plan references early, because they are harder to add later.

say: Project type is an Option field, so Residential never becomes residental. Featured is a yes or no switch.

say: Then open Editor mode and act like the client. Add a very long title and an item with no image. Fix what breaks now, because the client will do exactly this in the first month.

panel.rule: Test like a client: a very long title, and an item with no image.

say: An interaction joins a trigger, like a click or scroll, to an action, like a fade. Good uses help people: a menu opening, an FAQ expanding, a short fade-in.
Poor uses get in the way. Phones cannot hover, so never hide text behind a hover. And content must be readable even if an animation does not run.

Give every field a visible label, and turn on reCAPTCHA. Collect only what you need. If you ask for names, phone numbers or emails, add a privacy note and a policy link. Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 sets duties here, so the client should take advice.
Then test every form on the live domain, and confirm the client actually receives the email.

panel.heading: Forms that work and respect privacy

say: The most common Webflow speed problem is oversized photos straight from a phone. For example, Ifeoma's home page has 6 images totalling about 14MB.

panel.heading: Ifeoma cuts her page weight
items: PageSpeed Insights flags 6 images, about 14MB
Hero: 6000px to 2000px, WebP, about 300KB
5 card photos: 1000px wide, about 600KB
Lazy load the cards; re-run the test

say: She resizes the hero to 2000px wide and converts it to WebP. About 5MB becomes about 300KB.

say: The card photos go from about 9MB to about 600KB.

say: Check colour contrast before you build.

301 redirects, DNS records, SSL on

say: To remember. Plan before you build, and get the plan approved. Put repeating content in the CMS and make it client-proof. Keep pages light for mobile data, accessible, and clearly titled. And test forms and the domain live before you say the site is done.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Sitemap, content model and style guide first
Repeating content belongs in the CMS
Help text and Option fields keep it client-proof
Resize images; check contrast and keyboard
Forms: minimal data, privacy note, live test
